The fastest way to start a product integration API is to generate one from pvarki/python-integration-template, a Copier template that renders a working FastAPI service with the rmapi callback contract already wired up.

Generate a new integration

The template uses the jinja2-time extension, so it must be installed alongside Copier and --trust must be passed to load extensions:

uvx --with jinja2-time copier copy --trust \
  https://github.com/pvarki/python-integration-template <path_where_to_create>

Questions Copier asks

From copier.yml:

Question Meaning
title_en English product title shown on the UI card
short_name Shortname / slug used in URLs and as the dict key
package_name Python package name (defaults to <short_name>rmapi)
description_en English short description (defaults to <title_en> integration)
app_port Internal port the app binds to (must be unique on the productnet network)
component_type How the integration appears in the UI: link, markdown, or component

The component_type choice changes what gets generated:

  • **link** — the product card links to an external URL (replace https://example.com in description.py).
  • **markdown** — adds api/proxy.py, serving per-user Markdown at POST /api/v2/clients/{language}/info.md, which the core rmapi proxies.
  • **component** — scaffolds a ui/ folder (a Module Federation React bundle) plus api/clientinfo.py for the per-user data feed; the build output is served by nginx at /ui/<short_name>/remoteEntry.js.

What template/ generates

The rendered project (paths shown relative to the project root) includes:

  • pyproject.toml — uv-managed project metadata and dependencies (depends on libpvarki).
  • Dockerfile — multi-stage build with builder_base, production, devel_build, test, and devel_shell targets. Production copies kw_product_init from pvarki/kw_product_init:latest.
  • docker/entrypoint.sh, docker/entrypoint-dev.sh, docker/container-init.sh — container startup and the hot-reload dev entrypoint.
  • src/<package_name>/app.py — the FastAPI factory get_app() (CORS locked to the deployment domain regex; mounts /api/v1 and /api/v2 routers).
  • src/<package_name>/config.py — get_manifest() reads /pvarki/kraftwerk-init.json (with a localmaeher fallback).
  • src/<package_name>/api/usercrud.py — the five mTLS-guarded lifecycle stubs (created, revoked, promoted, demoted, updated), each raising NotImplementedError.
  • src/<package_name>/api/description.py — the v2 description endpoint returning the ProductComponent for your chosen type.
  • src/<package_name>/api/healthcheck.py — GET /api/v1/healthcheck, returns healthy=True unconditionally until you add real checks.
  • proxy.py (markdown) or clientinfo.py + ui/ (component), conditional on component_type.
  • tests/ — pytest suite asserting the stub/example behaviour.
  • RASENMAEHER_SETUP.md — step-by-step wiring into the legacy docker-rasenmaeher-integration stack.

After generation

Copier prints the next steps (_message_after_copy):

cd <your-integration>
git init && git add -A && git commit -m "chore: scaffold from python-integration-template"
uv lock
# for a 'component' integration also: cd ui && pnpm install && cd ..

Then read the generated RASENMAEHER_SETUP.md for wiring into the stack.

Implement the stubs

The generated usercrud.py handlers raise NotImplementedError. Implement the events your product needs and acknowledge the rest:
return OperationResultResponse(success=True)

Likewise, fill in the real fi/sv titles and descriptions in description.py, make healthcheck.py check your real dependencies, and update the generated tests as you go.

Linting and versioning

  • pre-commit at the repo root handles parser-free checks; parser-required checks (ruff, mypy, prettier, eslint) run against rendered output via uvx --with nox nox -s lint.
  • Versioning uses bump-my-version: bump-my-version bump <patch/minor/major> (use show-bump to preview).

See Set up your dev environment (Docker Compose) or (Kubernetes) to run the generated service against a real stack, and Community & Standards (in Contribute to Project) for the org-wide tooling rules.
